<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-storage`, touching **50** documentable anchor(s).

**32** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5fb79bc010cc9ab749dc29bfe44c83ef19f3dd11`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (symbol, 51 pages)`, `/api/v1/data (route, 50 pages)`
- **14** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5fb79bc010cc9ab749dc29bfe44c83ef19f3dd11` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4cb6b86a84e957a68f6afe7ca05e905ace66348c` — the merge of head `4f6a91d1d8d65c48b7ff3aec8f446e1f5ebfd75c` into base `5fb79bc010cc9ab749dc29bfe44c83ef19f3dd11`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4cb6b86a84e957a68f6afe7ca05e905ace66348c && git checkout 4cb6b86a84e957a68f6afe7ca05e905ace66348c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5fb79bc010cc9ab749dc29bfe44c83ef19f3dd11 4f6a91d1d8d65c48b7ff3aec8f446e1f5ebfd75c && git checkout -B drift-repro 5fb79bc010cc9ab749dc29bfe44c83ef19f3dd11 && git merge --no-ff 4f6a91d1d8d65c48b7ff3aec8f446e1f5ebfd75c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5fb79bc010cc9ab749dc29bfe44c83ef19f3dd11
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5fb79bc010cc9ab749dc29bfe44c83ef19f3dd11` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## ACCEPT · 2026-11-12T23:13Z · head `4f6a91d1d8d65c48b7ff3aec8f446e1f5ebfd75c`

Verdict: **ACCEPT**: `Refs #32712 (item a)`, a partial landing. Tier S: no governed path, 1098 changed lines (`check-governed-merges --pr 32891`). The seat lands it, per the maintainer's standing order that lane seats review and land with pm-dispatch.

## 席位核对

1. **Shape:** draft PR to `main` whose first content line is `Refs #32712 (item a)`. No closing keyword sits on any open card. All files are in `packages/services/service-storage/` plus one changeset, inside the re-posted claim 6837170173.
2. **Premise measured:** the upload-link page was English in every deployment, and its post-upload refusals showed `error.message`. That text carried the lock's `RECORD_LOCKED:` prefix with the record title, and the object and field API names on a read-only refusal. Now the page and every refusal's `userMessage` follow `Accept-Language`, then the workspace `localization` default, then English, across all eleven platform-table languages with `lang`/`dir`. Refusal text is the producer's marked user text, else the page's sentence for the code, else the producer's text behind a localized lead-in. `error.message` loses only the producer's code prefix (the `/api/v1/data` door's rule). `error.code` and the success body are unchanged.
3. **Gates on this head:** 37 check-runs `success`, 18 `skipped`, none failed or pending. `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` are both `success`. K = 11 behind `origin/main`. That is under 15, and main's locale changes in that span modify existing `ui/packages/i18n` packs (no new pack, and none this PR reads), so no merge before queueing.
4. **Accepted deviations:** a refusal code the page has no sentence for shows the producer's text behind the localized "the upload was refused" lead-in instead of a generic line, so validation reasons are not lost. Output safety was checked: every page sentence goes through `escapeHtml`, the script's strings are a `scriptLiteral` JSON literal (`<`, `>`, `&`, U+2028/9 escaped), and the status line is set by `textContent`.
5. **Out of scope:** acceptance (b) is whether the page names the record and field. That reverses the #30892 design choice, so it is a decision for a person. The card stays open for it and moves to `pm:needs-user-decision` after this lands. Changeset sentences were checked against the diff and are true at this head. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` hold: `userMessage` is an existing `ApiErrorSchema` member, and no export or schema moves.
6. **Landing:** `pr_ready`, then auto-merge through the merge queue. The seat follows the PR to MERGED, and #32712 stays open for (b).
